questions.question: Distinguish between real flows and money flows, giving one example of each in the factor market and one in the goods and services market.
questions.expected_answer: Real flows are flows of goods, services and factors of production; money flows are the payments for them, in the opposite direction. Factor market: labour flows from households to businesses (real); wages flow from businesses to households (money). Goods market: goods and services flow from businesses to households (real); consumption spending flows from households to businesses (money).

questions.question: Describe how the government is shown in the circular flow of a closed economy.
questions.expected_answer: The government buys factors (labour) from households in the factor market and pays salaries; buys goods and services from businesses in the goods market and pays for them; receives taxes directly from households and businesses; pays transfer payments (grants) directly to households and subsidies to businesses; provides public goods and services. Taxes and transfers are direct arrows, not through a market.

questions.question: Households earn R1 000 million, pay R200 million tax and save R100 million. Businesses invest R100 million and government spends R200 million. Calculate consumption, total leakages, total injections and total spending, and state what happens to the flow.
questions.expected_answer: Consumption = 1 000 - 200 - 100 = R700 million. Leakages = 200 + 100 = R300 million. Injections = 100 + 200 = R300 million. Total spending = 700 + 100 + 200 = R1 000 million, equal to income; leakages equal injections, so the flow stays steady.
